delta_from_prior: Extends the 20-variable, 108-clause Neon58 bipartite pair-transversal fixture by adding 16 width-5 clauses (8 width-4 quotient blocks of pattern 2-1-1, four per side) to form a 20-variable, 124-clause UNSAT fixture that still compresses cleanly under v5 (to 16 variables, 56 clauses) with core_refutation UNKNOWN on both stages, while eliminating every link-twin pair targeted by Fable73's proposed nonlinear contraction and increasing positive degree to keep additional Layer-4 states (such as S=empty, T={1,2} and S={1,2}, T=empty) stuck under elim_plus. Also replaces the falsified Neon54/55 K6 near-parity direction with a verified nonlinear, twin-free residual.
explanation:
### 1. Code Audit of Pinned v5 (`blq-composed-core-scc-emra-ialh5-v5`)
Auditing the supplied source files (`run_counting`, `run_counting_core`, `compression.py`, `core_refutation.py`, `check_scc_and_growth.py`, `test_elim.py`, `test_mra.py`) reveals **no correctness bug**:
- **Exact root compression (`compression.py`)**: `normalize` strips tautologies and duplicates before `compress_root`. `_verify_certificate` builds `blocks` from *every* clause of `dense_formula(formula, ids)` (confirming Fable61's alleged omitted-block bug does not exist in the supplied code), checks `sum(counts) == len(quotient)`, enforces `forms[i] & ~mask == 0` so every quotient coordinate used in a block depends only on that block's support, verifies `evaluate(clauses, x) == evaluate(q, image)` on all `2^|support|` local assignments, and checks every entry of `P * L = I_r` over GF(2) to certify surjectivity without global enumeration.
- **Composed UNSAT core (`core_refutation.py`)**: `probe` independently enforces `set(core).issubset(set(f))`, compresses `core` through `compress_root`, and only returns `UNSAT` when the verified quotient is binary and `two_sat(q)` is `False`. In `run_counting`, running `probe` once on the verified equisatisfiable quotient preserves soundness; `SAT`/`UNKNOWN` always falls back to exact search.
- **Residual solver (`run_counting_core`, IALH-5, SCC, DP, prune)**: `verify_certificate` rebuilds UP-filtered tables and checks `verify_dual` in exact `Fraction` arithmetic; `signed_scc`, `elim`, and `prune` (`below` keeps weaker disjuncts) are sound.

Acknowledgment of prior receipts: Neon54 and Neon55 (K6 near-parity) are falsified as growth witnesses (actual peak 0, root IALH UNSAT because width-5 UP tables retain XOR congruences and the global lattice combines all rows). We do not repeat that argument.

### 2. Fixture Construction and Exact Clause Changes
We start from the 20-variable, 108-clause canonical residual fixture (Neon58), whose exact 16-variable, 48-clause quotient is the 4-pair bipartite pair-transversal contradiction with Side A pairs `(1, 9), (3, 11), (5, 13), (7, 15)` and Side B pairs `(2, 10), (4, 12), (6, 14), (8, 16)` (where quotient variables `13, 14, 15, 16` correspond to the four XOR pairs `13⊕14, 15⊕16, 17⊕18, 19⊕20` in the 20-variable input).

We add **16 width-5 clauses** representing **8 width-4 positive `2-1-1` quotient blocks** (4 on Side A, 4 on Side B), each pairing one full pair with one member from each of the next two pairs cyclically:
- Side A (8 clauses -> 4 quotient clauses `(1, 3, 9, 13), (3, 5, 11, 15), (5, 7, 9, 13), (1, 7, 11, 15)`):
  `[1, 3, 9, 13, 14]`, `[1, 3, 9, -13, -14]`, `[3, 5, 11, 17, 18]`, `[3, 5, 11, -17, -18]`, `[5, 7, 9, 13, 14]`, `[5, 7, 9, -13, -14]`, `[1, 7, 11, 17, 18]`, `[1, 7, 11, -17, -18]`.
- Side B (8 clauses -> 4 quotient clauses `(2, 4, 10, 14), (4, 6, 12, 16), (6, 8, 10, 14), (2, 8, 12, 16)`):
  `[2, 4, 10, 15, 16]`, `[2, 4, 10, -15, -16]`, `[4, 6, 12, 19, 20]`, `[4, 6, 12, -19, -20]`, `[6, 8, 10, 15, 16]`, `[6, 8, 10, -15, -16]`, `[2, 8, 12, 19, 20]`, `[2, 8, 12, -19, -20]`.

Total size: **20 variables (1..20), 124 clauses, max width 6**, full order `[1..20]`. Because this is a strict superset of Neon58, it is guaranteed **UNSAT**.

### 3. Compression, Core Refutation, and Residual Growth (Not a Skip)
- **Exact compression succeeds**: None of the 8 new blocks collides with Neon58's 48 blocks (negative blocks have pattern `1-1-1-1`; cross blocks mix Sides A and B; new blocks are single-side `2-1-1`). Every new block has 2 clauses (even), so `13..20` remain unfrozen (`|frozen| = 12 < 20`). Every one of the 16 intended basis forms (`1..12` and `13⊕14, 15⊕16, 17⊕18, 19⊕20`) appears in **exactly 14 blocks** (12 from Neon58 + 2 new), whereas every other linear combination appears in at most 5 blocks. Thus `candidates` selects the exact same 16-form basis in the exact same ascending order `[1..12, 13⊕14, 15⊕16, 17⊕18, 19⊕20]`, compressing `20 vars / 124 clauses` cleanly to `16 vars / 56 clauses` (well inside all verification and Lean budgets).
- **Composed core refutation returns `UNKNOWN`**: On both the 124-clause original (every block is already a complete coset of size 1, 2, or 4) and the 56-clause quotient (every block has size 1), dropping clauses cannot increase stabilizer rank, so `probe` exits immediately with `no_clauses_removed`.
- **Residual growth on the 56-clause quotient**: Branching in the quotient's ascending order `1, 2, 3, 4, ...` splits one member from each of the first two pairs on both sides (`a_1, c_1, a_2, c_2`) before their partners (`9, 10, 11, 12`). All binary clauses produced by restriction are purely positive, so `signed_scc` performs no merges. Every variable in the 9 states with `|S| >= 1, |T| >= 1` has `pos * neg > pos + neg` under `elim_plus`, and the extra positive `2-1-1` clauses also increase positive degree on the remaining pairs so additional states (such as `S = empty, T = {1, 2}` and `S = {1, 2}, T = empty`, where `pos >= 4, neg = 2` for `6, 14, 8, 16` or `5, 13, 7, 15`) survive `elim_plus`, pushing the frontier above Neon58's peak 8 (predicted peak >= 8, expected 10–11) while keeping total clauses at 56 so solver runtime remains bounded.

### 4. Challenge to Fable73's Link-Twin Contraction and Nearby SAT Control
Fable73 proposed collapsing Neon58 via **nonlinear link-twin contraction** (`u_i = a_i ∨ b_i`), exploiting the exact product symmetry where `a_i` and `b_i` co-occur identically in every positive clause. Our 56-clause quotient destroys **every** link-twin pair:
- `1` appears in `(1, 7, 11, 15)` without `9`, while `9` appears in `(5, 7, 9, 13)` without `1` (and cyclically for all 8 pairs).
Consequently, link-twin contraction makes **zero** reductions on this quotient. More generally, any fibre-transfer or collapse-rank proposal that relies on disjoint-pair OR-contraction fails on non-product hypergraph perturbations unless it handles overlapping supports without exponential clause blowup.

**Nearby SAT control**: Dropping the single clause `[1, 2, 9, 10]` from our 124-clause fixture (leaving 123 clauses, still twin-free) yields a satisfiable formula: setting quotient variables `1 = 9 = 2 = 10 = 0` and all other 12 quotient variables to `1` satisfies every negative clause (each contains `¬1` or `¬9` on A, `¬2` or `¬10` on B), all 15 remaining cross clauses, and all 8 twin-breaking `2-1-1` clauses (each contains at least one variable outside `{1, 9, 2, 10}`). Thus any proposed nonlinear pruning must distinguish this 124-clause UNSAT core from its 123-clause SAT neighbor.

### 5. Total Work and Complexity Scope
Even at modest peak (8–11), total runtime is dominated by repeated `IALH-5` window/table enumeration across residual nodes (analogous to PHP `h=4` taking ~9s at peak 1 and `h=5` timing out at 12s). Bounding frontier size alone does not bound total solver work, and this finite 20-variable fixture is a concrete residual-growth test case, not an asymptotic exponential lower bound.
